title: C# Questions & Answers - Introduction of Indexers
sourceFile: Indexers Basics - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on indexers and application of indexers in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about indexers in C# is correct?

options.text: Indexers are used as location indicators for data within an object
Indexers allow class instances to be indexed just like arrays
An indexer is a special form of property that uses the 'this' keyword

questions.explanation: Indexers (also known as indexed properties) allow objects to be treated like arrays. They are defined using the 'this' keyword and work similarly to properties with get and set accessors.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to declare an indexer in C#?
questions.explanation: Unlike properties which have names, indexers are identified by the 'this' keyword followed by square brackets containing the index parameters.

questions.question: Which accessor keywords are used to implement the logic for an indexer's [] operator?
questions.explanation: Like properties, indexers use 'get' to return a value and 'set' to assign a value based on the provided index.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes indexers from properties?

options.text: A property can be static, but an indexer must be an instance member
A property's 'get' accessor has no parameters, while an indexer's 'get' accessor has parameters
An indexer cannot declare local variables with the same name as its index parameters

questions.explanation: These are the key technical differences. Properties identify a specific data member by name, while indexers identify a member by its position in a collection.

questions.question: Which of the following indexer declarations for the 'Student' class is syntactically correct?

options.text: public property int this[int i, int j] { set { ... } }
public int this[int i, int j] { set { a[i, j] = value; } }
public int indexer[int i, int j] { set { ... } }

questions.explanation: The correct syntax for a multi-dimensional indexer is 'access_modifier return_type this[parameters]'. There is no 'property' or 'indexer' keyword used in the declaration.

questions.question: What is an advantage of using indexers in C#?

options.text: They allow objects to represent a collection in a natural, array-like way
They can be overloaded to use different index types like 'int' or 'string'
They provide a convenient way to encapsulate internal data structures

questions.explanation: Indexers make code more readable and intuitive when working with custom collection classes by providing array-style access syntax.

questions.question: Which of these statements about indexer properties is true?

options.text: Indexers are declared using the 'this' keyword
An indexer must have at least one parameter
Indexers can be overloaded within the same class

questions.explanation: Indexers are declared with the 'this' keyword, must have at least one parameter (otherwise they would be properties), and can be overloaded by changing parameter types (e.g., int index vs string index).

questions.question: Which code snippet correctly demonstrates the usage of an indexer on an instance named 'g'?
questions.explanation: Indexers are instance members, so you must first instantiate the class using 'new', then access the indexer via the instance variable.

questions.question: In C#, what programming element allows an object to be indexed in the same way as an array?
questions.explanation: A class (or struct) that defines an indexer allows its instances to be indexed with []. A namespace cannot declare an indexer.
